findings.text: _unreadable_snapshot's docstring claims the row carries the same keys a classified snapshot does so a fold reads it as a state change, but no test asserts that key parity; a divergence in the hand-built row would be silent.

justifications.durability: tests/test_one_unreadable_pointer_never_stops_the_tick.py:141-155 asserts state/classification, the exception type and the incident message, and the negative-control log shows the same cases failing when the guard is removed.
justifications.evidence: the gate command in the manifest is the literal text that ran and both arms plus the base-revision new-test log show non-zero failure at base against zero at head.
justifications.fit: the guard follows the surrounding per-row idiom of reckon/crew/station_store.py:861 and reuses the snapshot vocabulary (state/classification/recovery_classification) rather than inventing one.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/station_store.py:867 catches an exception from _watch_snapshot, prints the row on stderr and stores an unreadable snapshot, so the pass reaches every other pointer.
justifications.reuse: search over reckon/crew found no other unreadable-pointer snapshot builder; _unreadable_snapshot is the owner of that row shape and _stream_session's unreadable-stream catch at resumption.py:884 is extended rather than duplicated.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path in the diff lies under the declared write paths; no unrelated refactor accompanies the guard.

verdicts.diff: read commit by commit (single commit 4934628fae): guard plus _unreadable_snapshot in station_store.py, BackendError added to _stream_session's catch in resumption.py, a 174-line test file, and an evidence fragment.
